questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.

options.text: Will always affect
May not affect
Is caused by

questions.correctAnswerText: May not affect
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: If you must drive a school bus during high winds, you should:

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Increase your speed.
Reduce your speed.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when driving a school bus in high winds. Hold the steering wheel firmly and watch for wind gusts.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Has a single air brake system with two sets of controls.
Has one air brake system for each side of the truck.
Has two brakes for each wheel.
Has two separate air brake systems with one set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has two separate air brake systems with one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems that share one set of controls. One system works the rear brakes. The other system works the front brakes.

questions.question: A passive railroad crossing:

options.text: Has a control device.
Does not have any control devices.
Should be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not have any control devices.
questions.explanation: A passive railroad crossing has no traffic control devices. The driver must decide whether it is safe to cross.

questions.question: Small amounts of hazardous material may be transported on a bus if:

options.text: The driver gets paid extra.
There is no other way to transport the material.
The passengers are notified in advance.
There is no bad weather in the forecast.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no other way to transport the material.
questions.explanation: Small amounts of hazardous materials may be carried on a bus only if there is no other way to transport them. Some materials cannot be carried on a bus under any circumstances.

questions.question: When leaving a vehicle unattended, a driver should:

options.text: Always set the parking brake.
Only set the parking brake if the vehicle is parked on a slope.
Deflate the tires by 10 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always set the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, exiting your vehicle incorrectly will result in:

options.text: Failure of only that exercise.
An extra point against your final score.
Automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: Automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: You must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact when exiting. On a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly means you automatically fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: If an air compressor is belt-driven, the belt should be checked to ensure that it is:

options.text: Thin.
Properly tightened.
Cracked.

questions.correctAnswerText: Properly tightened.
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor drive belt before each trip. Check that it is tight and not damaged.

questions.question: Baggage and freight should be stored so that:

options.text: Riders can exit by any door or window in an emergency.
An exit can be blocked if another exit is available.
Items partially cover a door since they can be moved aside.
Cargo can be easily removed in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders can exit by any door or window in an emergency.
questions.explanation: All baggage and freight must be stored so that the driver can move freely, riders can exit through any door or window in an emergency, and items will not injure riders if they shift or fall.

questions.question: When arriving at a destination, remind exiting passengers to take their carry-on bags:

options.text: Before you stop the bus.
After you stop the bus.
At least five times.
As they exit the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you stop the bus.
questions.explanation: Before the bus comes to a complete stop, remind passengers to take their carry-on bags with them.

questions.question: After starting a trip while transporting cargo, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to inspect the cargo.
You only need to inspect the cargo if someone tells you there is a problem.
You should inspect the cargo within 50 miles of starting the trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should inspect the cargo within 50 miles of starting the trip.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a school bus stop?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Drive slowly.
Talk to students on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly.
questions.explanation: Always approach school bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: When stopping at a railroad crossing, what happens if you open the front door?

options.text: It helps you hear an approaching train better.
You should never do this.
Other noises enter the bus, making it harder to hear a train.
It takes too long and is not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you hear an approaching train better.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, open your front door if it helps you see or hear a train coming.

questions.question: When checking tires during your vehicle inspection, what should you look for?

options.text: The inside of the tire should be more worn than the outside.
The outside of the tire should be more worn than the inside.
The middle of the tire should be more worn than the outside.
The tire should have even wear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tire should have even wear.
questions.explanation: Your tire tread should be worn evenly across the entire tire.

questions.question: When should a bus be refueled?

options.text: With passengers on board.
Without passengers on board.
In the evening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Without passengers on board.
questions.explanation: Do not refuel your bus while passengers are on board unless absolutely necessary. Never refuel with passengers inside an enclosed building.

questions.question: What is true about dry bulk tanks?

options.text: They usually have low centers of gravity.
They usually have high centers of gravity.
They are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.
They cannot be driven on interstates.

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and need careful driving. The material inside can shift during travel, which changes how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, what happens?

options.text: You do not have to do anything about railroad crossings.
The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would cross one at a practice location.

questions.question: When should the bus start moving after students board?

options.text: As soon as students are through the door
When students are close to their seats but still standing
When students are seated and looking forward
As soon as students cross the standee line

questions.correctAnswerText: When students are seated and looking forward
questions.explanation: Wait until all passengers are seated and looking forward before you move the bus.

questions.question: How should pre-trip inspections be done?

options.text: Differently each time so you focus on different items.
The same way each time so you do not forget anything.
Only once in a while.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you do not forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you learn all the steps and makes sure you do not skip anything.

questions.question: When traveling between states, which law applies to securing loads and vehicle weight?

options.text: The law of the state where the trip started.
The law of the state where the vehicle is located.
The driver should ask for federal rules to override state laws that conflict.
The driver can choose which state's law to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The law of the state where the vehicle is located.
questions.explanation: Vehicle weight, load securing, and where large vehicles can drive are regulated by federal, state, and local laws. These rules vary by location. Follow the laws of the state where you are driving.
